testCase.description: DMN 1.6 §11.2 example table: "a" = 1 -> FEEL null, B-FEEL false. DMN 1.6 §11.2 "In B-FEEL boolean operators ( =, <=, <, >, >=, not(), and, or, in, between ) always return a true or false result (never null)" / "an incompatible type in a boolean expression is considered false with the exception of the not equal (!=) where it is considered true."

DMN 1.6 §11.2 (derived): not() never returns null in B-FEEL. FEEL Table 52 'otherwise' gives null here; B-FEEL gives false (same as the spec's not("a")). DMN 1.6 §11.2 (derived): operand order swapped vs the spec's true and "x". FEEL Table 51 row otherwise/true gives null; B-FEEL gives false. DMN 1.6 §11.2 "In B-FEEL boolean operators ( =, <=, <, >, >=, not(), and, or, in, between ) always return a true or false result (never null)" / "an incompatible type in a boolean expression is considered false with the exception of the not equal (!=) where it is considered true."

DMN 1.6 §11.1 "Anything not covered in this chapter has the behavior described for FEEL" (derived): FEEL Table 51 row otherwise/true already gives true (no error), so B-FEEL also gives true; B-FEEL must not force false where FEEL is non-null.
DMN 1.6 §11.1 (derived): FEEL Table 51 row false/otherwise already gives false, B-FEEL keeps false. Same result in FEEL and B-FEEL.

DMN 1.6 §11.2 (derived): in with a list of positive unary tests; in FEEL "a" = 1 and "a" = 2 are null, so the result is null; B-FEEL gives false. DMN 1.6 §11.1 "null is used only to represent missing data" + Table 50 rule 49.a "null = e: FEEL(e) is null" (derived): FEEL already gives true, B-FEEL keeps true.
DMN 1.6 §11.1 + Table 50 rule 49.a "e = null: FEEL(e) is null" (derived): FEEL already gives false, B-FEEL keeps false.
